papers.title: Depth-progressive 3D seismic velocity model building via 2D generative diffusion models
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) velocity model building (VMB) remains computationally challenging with conventional approaches and native 3D neural networks, largely due to the prohibitive memory and training cost of full 3D formulations. Therefore, we introduce a depth-progressive framework that achieves 3D VMB using 2D generative diffusion models through a depth-as-channel formulation, in which the depth dimension of each 3D velocity patch is mapped to the channel dimension of a 2D U-Net. This allows the model to synthesize overlapping depth patches sequentially from shallow to deep while conditioning the prediction of the deeper patch on the shallower one, as well as on any available geophysical constraints, including well logs and structural attributes. During training, paired shallow-deep patch pairs with randomized overlaps are used to teach the network how deeper velocity structures relate to shallower information, and a classifier-free guidance strategy enables the model to handle missing constraints gracefully. At inference, starting from a shallow velocity prior, the model recursively generates deeper patches in a top-down manner, and a depth-attenuated Gaussian blending scheme merges overlapping predictions into spatially coherent 3D volumes while accounting for the progressive accumulation of uncertainty at greater depths. Numerical experiments on both in-distribution benchmark models, including Overthrust, SEAM Arid, and SEG/EAGE, and the out-of-distribution Marmousi model demonstrate that the method effectively propagates shallow velocity priors downward and produces high-quality 3D velocity volumes across a range of geological settings and conditioning scenarios. Compared to a 3D benchmark of equivalent architecture, the proposed method significantly reduces parameter count, training cost, and inference cost, while maintaining superior VMB accuracy.

papers.title: Event-Centric Earthquake Monitoring with a Multi-Station Transformer
papers.abstract: Earthquake catalogs underpin studies such as fault structure, earthquake processes and seismic hazard, and their value depends on being both complete and reliable. Machine learning has improved individual tasks of earthquake monitoring, but processing stations independently discards the consistency of arrivals across the network, and running tasks in sequence fragments the information describing each earthquake. We present EQNet2, a geometry-aware multi-station Transformer that jointly predicts phase arrivals, first-motion polarities, source location and magnitude, and the association of arrivals into events. On a Northern California test dataset and on continuous waveforms from Ridgecrest and the San Francisco Bay Area, EQNet2 recovers more weak arrivals, produces fewer false detections, and associates more picks into located events. Its learned attention links information across stations along time--distance patterns consistent with seismic moveout. As seismic networks grow denser, exploiting multi-station coherence and event-centric prediction offers a path to more complete and reliable catalogs.

papers.title: Full Waveform Inversion with a Learned Preconditioner
papers.abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful approach for reconstructing subsurface velocity models, but its practical performance is limited by ill-conditioning, sensitivity to the update direction, and the high cost of curvature-based methods. In this project, we investigate whether a neural operator trained on reverse-time-migration (RTM) images can provide a useful learned preconditioner for FWI. We compare projected FWI against neural-preconditioned FWI using either a standard Fourier neural operator (FNO) or a Jacobian-informed FNO (JI-FNO). The neural preconditioner applies the normal operator of the learned RTM map to modify the true Devito FWI gradient. Our experiments show that the JI-FNO preconditioner achieves the lowest model error while maintaining data-residual decay comparable to baseline projected FWI. In contrast, the standard FNO preconditioner is unstable and gives worse model recovery, despite using the same neural-preconditioning framework. We also identify a failure mode of a nonlinear neural Gauss Newton-type inner solve: directly matching the neural RTM output to the FWI gradient creates an objective-space mismatch and does not yield a reliable descent direction. These results suggest that forward RTM-image prediction alone is insufficient for learned preconditioning; accurate learned derivatives and objective-consistent use of the neural operator are critical for producing useful inversion updates.

papers.title: Sensitivity Fidelity Reveals Physical Dependencies Beyond Forecast Accuracy in Deep-Learning Earth-System Models
papers.abstract: Deep-learning models increasingly rival numerical simulation in Earth-system forecasting, yet forecast error alone cannot determine whether their learned input-output dependencies are physically consistent. Here we introduce sensitivity fidelity as an additional criterion: alongside prediction error, model responses to input perturbations should be examined against a trusted reference or established physical knowledge. In an idealized Rayleigh-B\'enard convection benchmark, four surrogate architectures achieved low forecast errors yet encoded markedly different sensitivities. Quantitative comparison with a matched adjoint distinguished the models far more sharply than forecast accuracy and showed that predictive skill and sensitivity fidelity need not coincide, while finite-perturbation experiments further linked these differences to the propagation of initial-condition uncertainty. We then applied this strategy to El Ni\~no-Southern Oscillation prediction, where no adjoint reference exists and learned sensitivities showed event-wise robustness, validity under finite perturbations, and consistency with established precursors. These results identify gradient-based evaluation as a discriminating complement to forecast-error metrics, providing a practical test of whether data-driven Earth-system models learn physically credible dependencies.

papers.title: CartoVec: General-Purpose Location Embeddings from Open Map Data
papers.abstract: Geographic coordinates are common inputs in applied machine learning, but latitude and longitude describe position rather than the surrounding environment. Image-grounded location encoders learn this context from satellite or ground-level imagery; structured open map data offers another source of supervision whose utility for continuous coordinate encoders remains less explored. We introduce CartoVec, a coordinate encoder trained to predict Overture-derived land cover, land use, transportation, place and connectivity targets at multiple spatial scales, without image inputs or downstream-task labels. We evaluate frozen embeddings on Census outcomes, Airbnb prices and Philadelphia crime in the US Northeast using spatial block cross-validation. CartoVec has the highest mean performance on most Census outcomes and the highest average across the full suite, with several comparisons close across folds. The findings support open map data as a practical source of reusable location representations with a coordinate-to-vector interface that requires no map lookup at inference. The open-weight model is available at https://huggingface.co/gursoyfurkan/CartoVec.

papers.title: A Spectral-Domain Pseudo-Inverse Method for True 3D Gravity Inversion
papers.abstract: The main difficulty in 3D gravity inversion is that surface observations lack vertical wavenumber information, making the problem underdetermined and depth resolution poor. Building on the author's spectral-domain pseudo-inverse theory for unitary diagonalizable systems, this paper presents a true 3D inversion method. Surface data are analytically continued upward via Laplace's equation to form a 3D data volume, providing the vertical wavenumber sampling for the 3D Fourier transform. A general analytical expression for the half-space spectrum is derived, separating the horizontal spectrum from the vertical propagation kernel. The Green's function of the 3D Poisson equation is unitarily diagonalized, yielding the forward spectral response $\lambda(\kk) = -i 4\pi G k_z / K^2$, and a stable inverse filter $q_\alpha(\lambda) = \bar{\lambda}/(|\lambda|^2 + \alpha)$ is constructed. This filter is proved to have bounded stability and consistency (reducing to the exact inverse as $\alpha \to 0^+$). Validation with a homogeneous sphere model shows correct recovery of the anomaly location and singular behavior at the source. The contributions are twofold: (1) upward continuation constructs a 3D volume from 2D surface data, which does not add physical observations but unfolds the 3D spatial variation information (data innovation) derived through the governing physical equation; (2) the inversion is reduced to one forward 3D Fourier transform, one spectral scaling, and one inverse transform. The framework extends to any linear potential-field inverse problem with a translation-invariant forward operator, including magnetic inversion.

papers.title: Planar intrusions from a narrow, jet-like source in a linearly stratified ambient
papers.abstract: We present two and three dimensional direct numerical simulations of planar intrusions injected from a continuously supplied, narrow source into a linearly stratified ambient at the level of neutral buoyancy. The evolution passes through three phases. A laminar leading vortex dipole first advances at constant speed with a varicose wave train behind it; the trailing jet then undergoes a sinuous instability whose initial growth rate and wavelength agree with inviscid unstratified planar-jet theory evaluated on the local jet; the flow finally relaxes into a buoyancy-controlled wedge whose area grows linearly in time. Three-dimensional simulations show that the transition remains organized by the planar instability, while three-dimensionality reshapes the near-source region into a slowly evolving, actively mixing zone that entrains an additional twenty to one hundred percent of the source flux depending on source width. Rescaled with this measured effective flux, the downstream intrusion collapses reasonably well onto the similarity solution for a wide-source intrusion.

papers.title: A semi-infinite hydraulic fracture propagating in a poroelastic medium
papers.abstract: We solve the near-tip coupled hydromechanical problem of a hydraulic fracture propagating in a permeable poroelastic medium, represented locally as a semi-infinite crack moving at constant velocity. In the moving tip frame, all fracture fields are steady. The porous solid obeys linear poroelasticity, fracture propagation follows LEFM, fluid flow within the tensile fracture is governed by lubrication theory, and the fracturing and pore fluids are treated as identical Newtonian liquids. The primary unknowns are the fracture opening and the fluid displacement function along the fracture, determined from the resulting non-linear system of equations. In a viscosity--toughness scaling, the problem depends on four dimensionless parameters: a dimensionless permeability $\varrho$ (associated with the intensity of fluid leak-in), a dimensionless effective confining stress $\Sigma_0'$ (measuring the relative importance of fluid leak-off and leak-in), the drained--undrained Poisson's ratio contrast $\beta$, and the poroelastic stress coefficient $\eta$. The solution evolves from a drained, toughness-dominated near-tip asymptote with uniform net pressure to an undrained, storage-viscosity-dominated far-field asymptote. Numerical solutions are obtained over parameter ranges representative of various rock types. The fully coupled model is compared with simplified models, namely uncoupled and one-way coupled formulations, over distances from the fracture front spanning laboratory-to-field scales. The resulting relative difference maps in the $(\varrho,\Sigma_0')$ parameter space identify four characteristic regimes: negligible poroelastic effects, dominance of the direct mechanical poroelastic response, importance of the poroelastic backstress, and a fully coupled regime. The latter occurs mainly at large $\varrho$ and small $\Sigma_0'$, corresponding to strong leak-in relative to leak-off.

papers.title: Earthquake Dynamics as a Benchmark for Scale-Invariant Behavior
papers.abstract: We analyze regional earthquake energy statistics from the Southern California and Japan seismic catalogs and find scale-invariant energy distributions characterized by an exponent $\tau \simeq 1.67$. To quantify how closely scale-invariant dynamics with different exponent values resemble real earthquakes, we generate synthetic energy distributions over a wide range of $\tau$ under conditions of constant activity. Earthquake-like behavior, in a broad sense, is obtained for $1.5 \leqslant \tau < 2.0$. When energy variations are further restricted to be within a factor of ten relative to real earthquakes, the admissible range narrows to $1.58 \leqslant \tau \leqslant 1.76$. We identify the physical mechanisms governing the dynamics in the different regimes: fault dynamics characterized by a balance between slow energy accumulation and release through scale-free events in the earthquake-like regime; externally supplied energy relative to a slowly driven fault for $\tau < 1.5$; and dominance of small events in the energy budget for $\tau > 2$

papers.title: Multivariate phase-space interpretation of ensemble forecasts: A comparison of physical and AI models
papers.abstract: Ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF's Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-ENS) are compared using a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Within this framework, the uncertainty is interpreted as the linear subspace spanned by the ensemble members in phase space, from which various geometric properties are extracted. As revealed by the analysis, the error does not entirely lie in this subspace, but is reasonably well calibrated in all directions. Moreover, the framework allows to quantify that this subspace critically depends on the number of ensemble members, suggesting that the current setups only partially represent the uncertainty subspace. This phase-space interpretation furthermore allows a direct comparison of the error-representation patterns of AIFS-ENS and IFS by computing the principal angles between the subspaces: IFS and AIFS ensemble subspaces do not entirely overlap in phase space, even though they were shown to have similar abilities to represent the amplitude and the structure of the error.

papers.title: Some generalizations of the tornado model
papers.abstract: A possible mechanism of tornado generation is associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability. The supercooled cloud-air mixture near the axis starts to descend and, due to the super adiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated near-surface air mass rises. The complete system of equations for full model includes equations for the stream function, for the azimuthal velocity component, and for the change in density. The refined model considers rotating convection within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics. The simplest model uses a separate equation for the stream function and can be applied to the initial stage of vortex generation. Within the framework of the simplest model, an analytical solution is combined from 8 linear dependencies by height. Rotation increases due to the conservation of angular momentum. Within the framework of the refined model, some unidirectional differential rotation arises, but it depends on boundary conditions (can be local). The full model studies the tornado development as rotating convection from the very beginning to the quasi-stationary stage. Velocity components increase in a coordinated manner. Two cases are considered: a single whirlwind and a two-eyed tornado. Radial flows converge towards the central part of the tornado near the earth surface, and there is an outflow from the "wall" to the axis and to the periphery near the top of the tornado. The maximum vertical velocity component is achieved at a certain radial distance at a certain height. The maximum azimuthal velocity component is achieved in the tornado "wall". Tornado generation criteria are discussed.

papers.title: Bayesian Inversion Beyond the Generator's Range: Reducing Non-physical Constraints from Generative Neural Networks
papers.abstract: To address non-uniqueness in geophysical inversions, Generative Neural Networks (GNNs) are often used to parameterise geological or other prior information in a lower-dimensional space (the so-called latent space), thereby reducing the number of inversion parameters. However, the training samples that represent this information are then always incorrect, because Earth structure is not intrinsically low-dimensional, and all GNNs are subject to training errors. Consequently, even when solutions are mapped back to the original higher-dimensional space, they inherit this imperfection and remain restricted to a low-dimensional manifold. From a mathematical point of view, latent space inversion thus fails fundamentally: generally, it can not even reproduce the best, higher-dimensional approximation to the true Earth. To overcome this limitation, we introduce an `escaping prior' distribution, which provides the necessary freedom to find solutions beyond the manifold of GNN-generated solutions, while still using the GNN as a guide. We use a hierarchical Bayesian approach to adapt the strength of prior information to the observed data and synthetic forward function $\textit{a posteriori}$. We illustrate our method on low-dimensional problems where the escaping prior is defined over a 1D manifold in 2D space. We then compare our approach with standard latent space and model space inversions using a uniform prior distribution in synthetic tomography problems, ranging from simple to more geologically realistic cases. Furthermore, we tested scenarios where the true solution is either far from or close to the manifold. In each case, our escaping prior shows significantly better results than the alternatives. It results in solutions beyond each GNN's generative capabilities, solutions which include the best possible model, and clearly demonstrates the limitations of latent space inversion.

papers.title: Latent Diffusion Modeling of Two- and Three-dimensional Fracture Networks with Sparse Observation Conditioning
papers.abstract: Characterizing subsurface fracture networks is challenging because geometry and connectivity are sparsely observed and uncertain away from measurements. We develop a latent diffusion framework for unconditional and observation-conditioned generation of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) fracture networks. Fractures and the surrounding matrix are represented as binary fields and compressed by a variational autoencoder into compact spatial latent representations, where an Elucidated Diffusion Model learns their distribution. The 3D model operates on native volumetric fields, with a reconstruction objective designed to preserve sparse, thin fracture structures. Sparse borehole observations are incorporated through a conditioning encoder, classifier-free guidance, and diffusion posterior sampling. Generated ensembles reproduce key fracture-network statistics, including fracture area/volume fraction, two-point correlation, and chord-length distributions. Reconstructed fracture counts and gas-production responses are comparable to those of the reference networks under the considered multiphase flow scenarios. Conditional generation satisfies 99.6% of prescribed well observations in 2D. In 3D, where vertical boreholes constrain full voxel columns, conditional realizations satisfy 84.2% of observed well voxels while maintaining fracture volume and geometry comparable to the reference ensemble. These results demonstrate the potential of latent diffusion models as compact probabilistic representations for fracture-network characterization, ensemble generation, and sparse-observation conditioning.

papers.title: Global Structure-Constrained 4D prestack inversion
papers.abstract: Prestack seismic inversion often suffers from inherent ill-posedness and is significantly affected by complex factors such as the wavelets, parameter coupling, heterogeneous media, fault displacements, and stratigraphic variations, making it difficult for the conventional inversion methods to accurately recover subsurface information. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a global inversion method based on multi-dimensional matrix multiplication to optimize the inversion results under structure constraints. This method first represents the inversion model as a four-dimensional tensor representing spatial and parameter dimensions. By performing multi-dimensional matrix multiplication operations in various directions of the model, a multi-dimensional tensor of observed data is effectively constructed. Secondly, multi-dimensional regularization are introduced. By analyzing the impact of different dimensional constraints on the inversion results, targeted parameter selection and adjustment are achieved, significantly enhancing the stability of the inversion process and effectively suppressing noise. Finally, stratigraphic and fault constraints extracted from seismic interpretation are incorporated to improve the geological coherence and reasonableness of the inversion results. Both synthetic and field data experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enhances the robustness of inversion in complex structural areas while maintaining high computational efficiency, validating its effectiveness in practical applications.

papers.title: Chemical transport by weakly nonlinear internal gravity waves in stars
papers.abstract: While internal gravity waves (IGWs) are known to transport chemicals in the radiative zones of stars, substantial uncertainty remains regarding the magnitude and physical mechanisms of this transport. Most previous studies have relied on heuristic theories or numerical simulations that are difficult to extrapolate to stellar parameters. In this work, we present the first rigorous asymptotic calculation of (passive) chemical transport by IGWs, in the limit of small wave amplitude. The net vertical transport induced by a coherent packet of waves is found to be proportional to the horizontal mean of $(w^S+w^E)^2$, where $w^S$ and $w^E$ are the vertical Stokes and Eulerian mean velocities. The transport scales as the fourth power of wave amplitude and quadratically with time, and we verify these scalings with numerical simulations. In the weakly damped regime, the dominant transport coefficients scale as $\omega^{-2}\kappa^2$, where $\omega$ is the wave frequency and $\kappa$ is the radiative diffusivity. Because the transport can be positive or negative depending on the wave phases, the effective mixing induced by the superposition of coherent wave packets is expected to scale with the eighth power of wave amplitude. These results provide a theoretical foundation for making accurate predictions of IGW-induced chemical transport in stellar evolution models.

papers.title: Design and Implementation of a 25-Yr Pseudoprospective Earthquake Forecasting Experiment in China (AoyuX)
papers.abstract: Forecast models in statistical seismology are commonly evaluated using log-likelihood (LL) scores for the full distribution $P(n)$ of earthquake counts. However, fat tails and out-of-range observations (realized counts exceed all simulations) can bias model rankings. We develop a tail-aware framework that estimates cell-wise $P(n)$ using adaptive Gaussian kernel density estimation and compares three treatments of out-of-range counts: power-law extrapolation, a fixed minimum probability, and exclusion. Using the AoyuX platform, we conduct a 25-year (2000--2023) month-by-month pseudoprospective experiment in the China Seismic Experimental Site. We compare an epidemic-type aftershock sequence model with a homogeneous background, ETAS$\mu$, with a spatially heterogeneous variant, ETAS$\mu(x,y)$, across six spatial resolutions and five magnitude thresholds, using 100,000 simulations per forecast window. Count distributions follow power laws, $P(n) \sim n^{-(1+a)}$, with $a \approx 1.02 \pm 0.23$, yielding a productivity exponent $\alpha = 0.83 \pm 0.19$ for $b = 0.85 \pm 0.002$. Model rankings depend on tail treatment: power-law extrapolation is theoretically justified and empirically most robust, whereas occasional advantages of the fixed-probability approach in coarse, low-magnitude settings are attributable to noise. Cumulative information gain shows that ETAS$\mu(x,y)$ outperforms ETAS$\mu$ in data-rich configurations, especially for $M_t = 3.0$--$3.5$ and whole-region tests. Positive mean information gain is concentrated where earthquakes with $M \geq 5$ occurred, whereas stochastic fluctuations dominate data-poor settings. A coefficient-of-variation analysis distinguishes genuine upward trends from noise. The framework supports statistically grounded evaluation of earthquake forecasting models.

papers.title: Enhanced Seismicity Monitoring in the Rapid Scientific Response to the 2025 Santorini Crisis
papers.abstract: We used a deep learning workflow to enhance earthquake detection during the 2025 seismic unrest between Santorini and Amorgos islands to track the evolution of the crisis in near real-time. We analysed the continuous seismic waveforms daily (1/2 - 3/3/25) as the crisis unfolded. Our analysis enhanced the earthquake catalogue from around 4,000 to 80,000 earthquakes. The enhanced catalogue allowed this international expert group to identify the volcanic-tectonic character, clearly revealing burst-like, spasmodic seismicity swarms, which is a pattern associated with fluid-driven processes from early stages of the crisis. Detailed moment tensor inversions in early events characterised by a significant non-double couple component indicated the involvement of magmatic or high-pressure hydrothermal fluids driving the unrest. Concurrent DL-enhanced tomography efforts identified a third, deep magmatic reservoir beneath Anydros Islet, consistent with pressure-driven processes. To date, volcanic-tectonic swarms in which >200 earthquakes of ML > 4 occurred within only a few weeks, largely within episodic bursts of seismicity, have not been observed elsewhere.
